sessions.title: Reading Groups
sessions.description: Biweekly discussions of protocol literature. Each session takes one or two readings from the library and works through them together, usually with a guest.

sessions.title: Diagram Jams
sessions.description: Collaborative diagramming sessions: drawing research processes together, and arguing about how to represent agents, objects and the knowledge moving between them.

projects.title: Protocol Literature Collection
projects.description: Our shared reading list, kept as a public Zotero group: protocol practice across domains, from the life sciences and biomedicine to distributed networks and indigenous rights.

projects.title: Protocollage
projects.description: Assembling heterogeneous case studies out of ethnographic fieldwork artifacts. Next step: logging case studies directly on this site, from a template built on the metadata schema we maintain.

projects.title: Conference Crashing
projects.description: Members turn up at symposia and conference sessions, alone or in groups, to bring protocol questions into other fields' rooms.
projects.note: Most recently: Symposium 'The Life of Protocols in the Life Sciences', ISHPSSB 2025, Porto.

projects.title: SIG: Standardization & Variability in Biosciences
projects.description: A special interest group on standardization in the scientific practices, mostly the empirical and experimental ones: how standards hold together, and what varies underneath them anyway.

projects.title: SIG: Integral Protocol Theory
projects.description: A special interest group working towards an empirically-based transdisciplinary philosophy of protocolization

projects.title: SIG: Ethnography of the “Boring”
projects.description: Taking up Susan Leigh Star's provocation to study boring things, and working out the methods for it — somewhere between archival and documentary research and ethnomethodology.

projects.title: SIG: The Procedural Mind
projects.description: Where the micro-sociology of practice meets cognitive science and psychology: what following a procedure does to, and asks of, a mind.

projects.title: Protocol Studies Concept Cartography
projects.description: Mapping the conceptual space of protocol studies: definitions, characterisations, examples and the routes between ideas. Modelled on Concept Cartography, which grew out of a reading group on epistemic diversity and whose cartographers include two Protocollege members.

potentials.title: Citation Protocols Working Group
potentials.description: Working out how the collective cites, pins and credits the things it reads and makes.

potentials.title: Protocol Symposium Collaboration
potentials.description: Co-hosting a symposium with an allied group, rather than only crashing other people's.

potentials.title: Self-hosted sessions and recordings
potentials.description: Running our own video and archive, so sessions do not depend on anyone's institutional account.
